ai_provisions: Article 20.4(1): the Parties recognise that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and other digital technologies, are becoming increasingly important in the global economy and offer significant social and economic benefits.

Article 20.4(2): the Parties shall cooperate, where appropriate through the Strategic Innovation Dialogue, in activities that may include sharing research and industry practices, promoting responsible adoption, encouraging commercialisation, developing international standards, facilitating investment and promoting trade in emerging technologies.

Article 20.4(3): the Parties shall endeavour to collaborate on governance frameworks through relevant international fora, in particular the Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence, and to take into account the OECD Principles on Artificial Intelligence adopted on 22 May 2019.
relevance.excluded_scope: Chapter 20 is excluded from dispute settlement by Article 20.7. The AI clause creates no AI-specific prohibition, standard, market-access condition, enforcement mechanism or dedicated regulator.
relevance.reason: A binding bilateral free trade agreement in force with an express article on artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. The AI clause is cooperative and non-justiciable; the Agreement is not an AI-specific treaty.
